sentence: This project provides animal scanners that let researchers study how tumors grow and respond to therapies in animal models of cancer.
This project tries to find out what focal adhesion kinase acts on and how it controls the fusion of secretory vesicles in developing neurons.
This project studies how a calcium sensor in mitochondria affects aging, memory and brain health in a mouse model of accelerated aging.
This project studies how tissue microenvironments control how cancer starts, progresses and responds to treatment.
This project grows and shares human airway cells and tests how they work in cystic fibrosis lung disease.
This project studies how an inhibitory receptor that binds another molecule controls immune cell activation and responses against tumors.
This project tries to use exosomes loaded with mRNA to produce macrophages with a chimeric antigen receptor in the body against glioblastoma.
This project supports researchers who measure age-related changes in metabolism in animal models, from molecules and cells to the whole organism.
This project develops ways to bring precision medicine researchers, patients, families and clinicians together on shared values, using cerebral palsy research as an example.
This project tests whether rare genetic variants in protein-coding genes are linked to early-onset ischemic stroke, using exome-sequencing of adults with stroke and controls.
This project tries to find out how a gene linked to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders controls a signaling pathway in neurons.
This project tries to find out how a protein helps clear tau protein from neurons and why some neurons become vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease.
This project sets up a computational core that analyzes sequencing data to predict disease-causing genetic variants in inborn errors of immunity.
This project uses deep learning to design miniproteins and antibodies that block bacterial adhesins, as antibiotic-sparing treatments for infections caused by multidrug resistant bacteria.
This project analyzes large datasets to find out how sleep and sex-specific brain biology relate to the risk of depression in adolescence.
This project builds a virtual platform to assess how well medical imaging technologies work in clinical use.
This project studies how immune cells and tumor signals shape the response of lung adenocarcinoma to tyrosine kinase inhibitors in murine models and tumor specimens.
This project tries to find out how cells in the prelimbic cortex and dorsomedial striatum support model-based control, the ability to plan future choices.
This project tries to find out how a mutation in the angiotensin I converting enzyme gene causes neuron death and cerebrovascular dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease.
This project develops a topical tracer that lets retinal imaging cameras detect a protein linked to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia.
